strings: "For Love Eternal" is a tragic quest given by Cerellean Whiteclaw in Auberdine. Haunted by memories of his lost lover, Anaya Dawnrunner, Cerellean asks an adventurer to travel to the shattered ruins of Ameth'Aran to release her restless spirit from an eternity of torment.

Ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients, the catastrophe surrounding the Well of Eternity tore ancient Kalimdor apart. Among the casualties was the city of Ameth'Aran, where Cerellean Whiteclaw lost his beloved, Anaya Dawnrunner. Stricken with despair, Cerellean followed Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage into the long hibernation of the druids, hoping the millennia spent walking the Emerald Dream would quiet his aching heart. Instead, his sorrow only lingered, following him through the ages.

Upon awakening in recent times, Cerellean wandered through Darkshore in a stupor until his feet brought him back to the melancholy ruins of Ameth'Aran. There, wandering among the ancient stones, he beheld the tortured ghost of Anaya. Unable to bear raising a weapon against the woman he loved, he pleads with passing travelers to destroy her tormented manifestation, retrieve her pendant, and finally grant her troubled soul peace.

When Anaya's pendant is returned to Auberdine, a spectral remnant of Anaya appears before Cerellean one last time. Freed from the lingering anguish that bound her to the ruins, she shares a brief, silent goodbye before fading away into the ether, leaving the grieving druid to weep in bittersweet solace by the seaside.

The Great Outdoors is an introductory survival lesson offered by seasoned travelers to newly minted wanderers across Azeroth. By taking a moment to rest by a warm campfire, fledglings learn how staying well-rested and prepared keeps an adventurer alive beyond city walls. It marks the first step into mastering wilderness survival and specialized field camps.

No matter how sharp your blade or potent your magic, the wilds of Azeroth quickly whittle down anyone who neglects the basics of survival. Seasoned wanderers stationed near roadside clearings offer this simple lesson to travelers setting out from their home valleys. Taking time to rest by a campfire does more than ease sore boots—it settles the mind and readies the spirit for the harsh road ahead. Only those who master the discipline of regular rest and preparation stand a chance of surviving long enough to claim fortune and glory.

Once an adventurer grasps the value of a crackling fire and proper rest, the instructors point them directly toward town tradesfolk. A camp in the field is rarely complete with just an ember and a bedroll; survival requires practical crafts. Whether forging replacement rivets, cooking trail rations, or stitching torn gear under the stars, every profession provides unique camp fixtures to turn a barren hillside into a self-sufficient outpost.
